**ID:** Bu-Vb Np3

**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 3  
**Title (English, from literature):** Keeping extra robe-cloth beyond a month  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 3 (titled *Akālacīvara*) regulates the storage of extra robe-cloth by Buddhist monastics. The rule stipulates that if a monk receives robe-cloth and retains it with the expectation of obtaining additional material to complete a set, he may keep the cloth for up to one month; keeping it beyond that period requires him to forfeit the robe-cloth and confess the transgression. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 The reference passages identified in secondary literature offer no direct analysis, consisting only of a misplaced volume/heading reference and a bare index entry [1, 2].
